title: Visits: booking and status
moduleTitle: App: Field service operations (proposed module; not in curriculum/structure yet)
audience: Owners and office staff who schedule, dispatch and record field jobs. No developer knowledge is needed.
learningOutcomes: Create a visit against a job with a window and an expected duration.
Name the visit status stages and say what moves a visit between them.
Explain why a visit's parent record matters.

instruction.heading: What a visit records
instruction.body: A visit is one planned trip to a site. It records when the work should start, how long it should take, which job it belongs to and who is assigned. Most visits sit under a job. A visit can also hang off an asset, a customer account, or a lead for a site survey. The parent shows the kind of visit it is. A job-linked visit covers the work itself, while an account-linked visit might be a general check.

instruction.heading: Status stages
instruction.body: A visit moves through stages: not yet scheduled, scheduled, dispatched, in progress, finished, unable to finish and cancelled. Changing a visit's status can trigger the next step, so make changes deliberately. If a visit is unscheduled, it goes back to not yet scheduled. A visit that cannot be finished should be marked unable to finish, with a reason recorded, so the office can plan a follow-up rather than lose the work. Status names can be renamed to suit your business, but the stage order does not change when you rename them.

procedure: Open the job and create a visit from it.
Set the window start, the window end and the expected duration.
Check the parent link and the visit type.
Save the visit as not yet scheduled, then schedule it once a worker and time are confirmed.
Move the status as the work happens, and note a reason whenever a visit cannot be finished.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner books a bond clean, but when they arrive the key is not there and the agent cannot be reached.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the visit be marked finished, unable to finish, or deleted?
workedExamples.reasoning: The work did not happen, so the visit is marked unable to finish with the reason recorded. A follow-up visit is then booked once the key is confirmed. Deleting it would remove the record of the attempt.

equipmentAndPpe: A device with the SkilledAt.Work Field app, where the lesson uses it

commonErrors.error: Marking a visit finished before its tasks are done.
commonErrors.prevention: Complete a visit only when its work and tasks are finished.

commonErrors.error: Leaving a visit in progress overnight.
commonErrors.prevention: End each day by moving every open visit to a clear status.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson covers app records and office process only. It does not grant, confirm or replace any licence, certificate or authority, and it makes no legal claim.

qualityStandard: Every visit has a parent job, a window and a duration.
Every unable-to-finish visit has a recorded reason.
summary: A visit is one trip and sits under a parent record.
The status stages show where the trip stands.
A visit that cannot be finished needs a recorded reason.

knowledgeChecks.question: A cleaner arrives but cannot start because a key is missing. What should the visit be marked as?
options: Completed and paid, with the invoice sent
Unable to finish, with the reason recorded
Cancelled without a note on the list

knowledgeChecks.question: Which stage means the trip is planned but not yet given a time and worker?
Why does the link from a visit to its parent matter?
options: It shows what kind of visit it is and what work it covers
It sets the worker's hourly pay rate for the week
It changes the visit's colour on the screen of the phone
